description: Dataset facts for the paneldx validation protocol: where each panel comes from, what licence it carries, how its correct entity key is known, and the sha256 of the exact bytes the suite is allowed to run on. Verdicts are not recorded here; regression expectations live in tests/validation/expected_results.json.

roles.development: Used while developing the rules and thresholds. Agreement on these panels is expected and is not evidence of accuracy.
roles.calibration: The only split on which thresholds may be fitted. Populated at manifest version 1.1.0.
roles.held_out: Registered for a single evaluation after the method is frozen. Never used for tuning and never fetched by default. Their structure and checksums are recorded here; paneldx has not been run on any of them.
roles.external: Reserved for cross-domain evaluation from outside econometrics. Empty at manifest version 1.1.0.
roles.case_study: Illustrative only. Never counted in any evaluation metric.

license.data_license_note: Restricted research data. No public licence exists to review.
license.redistribution_note: Never fetched by any script here. The manifest schema forbids a source_url on a restricted dataset.
license.verification: Access is governed by the holding researchers, not by a licence.

correct_key_evidence.detail: The true physician identifier is not known. `Disease + Opening time` is the best-supported candidate found by search, not established ground truth, so this dataset is a case study and is excluded from every evaluation metric in the protocol.

family_id: Datasets drawn from the same underlying source share a family_id. A family never spans two splits: two panels built from one survey would leak calibration information into a held-out result. Rates are also resampled by family rather than by dataset, which is the same thing while every family here contains exactly one dataset.

excluded_candidates.source: R package plm, dataset Wages (Cornwell and Rupert, PSID 1976-1982)
excluded_candidates.reason: The distributed CSV has no entity column and no time column: the panel index is implicit in row order (595 individuals x 7 years). A key reconstructed from row position is exactly the defect paneldx exists to detect, so the correct key is not documented and the dataset cannot supply ground truth.
The distributed CSV carries `id` but no time column, so the documented period cannot be recovered from the file.

Same family as the held-out dataset `usseatbelts`: both are US state-year traffic-fatality panels derived from FARS. Calibrating on one would leak into the other, and a family may not span two splits. The held-out slot was kept and this candidate dropped.

license_notes.data_license: Recorded as NOASSERTION wherever upstream does not state a licence for the data rows themselves. The Rdatasets maintainer says that licence could not be determined and believes the data free to redistribute, which is a belief rather than a grant, so the licence of the shipping package is recorded separately and not inherited.
license_notes.redistribution: No dataset is redistributed here. The data licence is unestablished and the shipping packages are GPL, which would not mix cleanly with this project's Apache-2.0 distribution. Files are fetched at validation time and verified by checksum.
license_notes.verification: verified_on and verified_from record when and where the upstream licence statements were read. This is a review of upstream claims, not an independent legal determination.
